senses.gloss: pr. n. m.Macrin, (supposed to mean) Macrianus, one of the thirty tyrants, who after the capture by the Persians of Valerian, was declared Roman emperor together with his sons Macrianus and Quietus.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 76:6">Gen. R. s. 76</cite> (ref. to ‘three of the older horns’, <cite ref="Daniel 7:8">Dan. VII, 8</cite>) <he>זו שנתנו להם מלכותם מ׳ וקרוס וקרדידוסי</he> (some ed. <cite ref="M02382"><he>מקדין</he></cite>) those (Romans) who gave them (the princes of Palmyra,) their royal titles (v. <he>נֵצַר</he> IV); M. &c.; Yalk. Dan. 1064 <he>מוקירוס וקירוס וקירקוס</he> (omitting <he>זו … מלכותם</he>) (some ed. <he>וקרירוס</he>; Fürst Gloss. Graeco-Hebr. p. 145 quotes: <he>וקירידיס</he>). [The other two names, obviously corrupted, refer perhaps to the two sons of Macrianus. V. Fürst l. c. for other conjectures.]
